key_insight: Neptuna is the first large-scale benchmark tailored to shock-driven compressible multiphase flows, showing that no single surrogate model or loss works best across all cases, but composite losses and SoftAdapt improve interface and spectral fidelity.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps engineers choose and validate machine learning surrogates for difficult multiphase problems such as bubble collapse and droplet breakup, where shocks, interfaces, and mixing must all be captured reliably.
method: Built a 2.4 TB benchmark with high-fidelity 2D and 3D datasets for shock-induced bubble collapse and droplet breakup.
Compared convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models.
Tested MSE, Sobolev, interface-aware, and structure-aware losses, plus SoftAdapt and GradNorm weighting.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, and the abstract reports that composite losses and SoftAdapt consistently improved interface preservation and spectral fidelity.
watch_item: Results may not transfer directly to new multiphase regimes or real 3D deployment settings, and the added loss terms can require careful tuning for stable training.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
